scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W023 anchor image confirms: the building is surrounded by neon yellow-green and orange verticals with a teal-blue upper zone and a pale blue-grey lower band — observations are accurate. The description 'neon yellow-green marks run vertically' is confirmed but the lower band is more teal-blue than pale blue-grey at full resolution; prose adjusted slightly.

W150 anchor image confirms: the composition shows golden hillsides, a blue river channel left of center, a green ridge form, and a teal-blue sky with black and white looping lines — the draft observation of 'dense overlapping black scribble lines layered over flat color' is accurate for the hillside areas. The sky upper zone is teal with loose black and white lines, not a simple flat color. Prose adjusted to reflect the sky zone.

W290 anchor image confirms: the image has a pale grey-pink upper zone (clouds), a warm amber-orange band, a broad turquoise sweep through the middle, and turbulent maroon/dark lower forms with white looping outlines. The draft description is accurate. The transition from W150 claiming 'same palette pushed toward dissolution' is partially supported — both share amber-gold and blue/teal — but W290 is far more turbulent and abstract while W150 retains legible landscape structure. Transition reworded to be more specific about visible differences.

W072 observations describe 'yellow clusters above dark branching and upright forms' and 'a low row of vertical divisions along the bottom edge.' The anchor image confirms this reads as a tree canopy scene. The transition from W290 to W072 (pressured horizontal zones giving way to vertical movement) is visually supported.

W064 observations describe horizontal white lines over vertical color strokes. The image confirms this. The transition from W072 (canopy yellow reappearing with ruled lines) is supported by both works sharing yellow-orange masses, though W064 is more abstract. Transition is accurate.

W046: the dark figure, white looping forms below, and warm solar disc upper-left are all confirmed in the image. The transition from W064 claiming 'soft yellow masses condense into a single disc' is a reasonable visible correspondence — both works share yellow-orange upper areas. Transition is acceptable.

W098: the large face on yellow-olive field with red-orange eye/mouth accents and white teardrop shapes is confirmed. The transition from W046 claiming 'solar disc has expanded into an entire yellow field' is a reasonable visible link between the warm upper-left disc in W046 and the yellow field in W098. Acceptable.

W133: the rounded head with black hatching, yellow loop arc, and visible teeth are confirmed. The transition from W098 is supported — both show faces under color-field pressure, with the shift from external color field to surface hatching being a genuine visible contrast.

W056: the draft describes this as a 'face-like reading' but the image shows no clear face — it is an abstract composition of light fan, gold/ochre bands, and a heavy black arc. The 'face-like reading' claim is unsupported and has been removed. The work's role is revised to focus on its abstract light-versus-weight dynamic as a contrast to the face works.
W153: the gold-olive mass, diagonal light beam, dark cavity, and background spirals are confirmed. The transition from W056 (light fan narrowing to a beam) is visually supported.
W196: the dome enclosure, gold rays, dark-blue form inside, and floating pale circles are confirmed. The transition from W153 (diagonal beam expanding to radial burst) is supported.

W183: the dark left mass, blazing yellow-gold right field with two white discs, and red blocks at bottom are confirmed. The transition from W196 (contained radiance opening into unenclosed split) is supported.

W041: the two diagonal light beams, nested rectangles, glowing ovals, and dense left scribble edge are confirmed. The transition from W183 (two white discs reappearing as two beams) is a reasonable visible link.

W190: the angular form with two white glowing rectangles, zigzag lines, and dark upper-left cluster are confirmed. The transition from W041 (beams condensing into fixed rectangular sources) is supported.

W219: the horizontal bar with oval recesses, downward triangles, and surrounding zigzag lines are confirmed. The transition from W190 (glowing rectangles becoming oval recesses in a bar) is a reasonable visible correspondence.
W224: the two diagonal beams, arched form with nested rectangles and glowing spiral cores, and olive-acid yellow-green field are confirmed. The transition from W219 is supported.

Chapter 3 title 'Faces Under Pressure' is inaccurate because W056 does not show a face — it is abstract. Chapter retitled to 'Faces and Fields' with W056 repositioned as a contrast stop showing a field without a face, making the chapter's progression more honest.
The W056 whyHere text claiming 'face-like reading of the composition' is unsupported by the image and has been corrected to describe the actual visible content.
Introduction mentions 'a river valley holds as much weight as any portrait' — this is a reasonable reading of W150 and W290 and is retained.
No invented objects, unsupported psychology, chronology or influence claims found beyond the W056 face-reading issue now corrected.

Repetitive language check: 'push-pull' appears in W133 and W190 readings — removed from W190 whyHere in visitor prose. 'Charged' appears multiple times but in different contexts; reduced where possible.
All 16 slots present exactly once. Chapter count is 5, within range.
evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study
evidence.wordingReviewScope: Text-only tightening of image-reviewed headings and invitations; no new image inspection or membership change
evidence.assistantWordingScope: Specificity and overstatement corrections to exhibition headings and invitations. Existing image-reviewed memberships, chapter order and artwork roles remain intact.
evidence.referenceExpansionMethod: Exact collection-plan slot to title and CID lookup; no new interpretation

title: Figures, Places and Light
question: When does the surrounding space become part of the subject?
introduction: Follow surroundings that attract attention alongside a figure: colored grounds, rays, shadow-like areas and landscape-like passages. Some drawings leave room around a recognizable subject; others cross its boundary with the same marks found in the setting. Compare the direction and scale of those marks before deciding which part of the image to follow.
closing: Look at an earlier setting after the final works. Which surrounding shapes now seem as useful for reading the image as the figure itself?

chapters.title: Grounds That Will Not Recede
chapters.introduction: Three works where the space beneath and around a form is as visually active as anything placed on it — the ground competes rather than supports.

stops.whyHere: A gabled building holds its shape through repeated misaligned outlines while neon yellow-green verticals and a teal lower band compete equally with the structure for attention.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #21

stops.whyHere: Golden hillsides, a blue river channel, and a teal sky built from looping black and white lines make the landscape itself the subject — no single form anchors the field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the building in the previous work was framed by charged marks, here those marks have spread across the entire surface with no structure left to contain them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #158

stops.whyHere: Turquoise sweeps and maroon hollows press against each other across three zones; white looping outlines hold the lower mass together without resolving it into any readable form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works share amber-gold and blue-teal areas, but here the landscape has become far more turbulent and abstract — the legible hillside gives way to churning, interlocked color masses.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #15

chapters.title: Canopy, Cloud, Open Air
chapters.introduction: Three works where marks accumulate into something sky-like or foliage-like, and the boundary between inside and outside becomes genuinely uncertain.

stops.whyHere: Yellow clusters spread above dark upright forms in an arrangement that can suggest trees, with translucent areas softening the boundary between support and canopy.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: After the turbulent horizontal zones of the previous work, the vertical movement here — dark forms rising into spreading yellow — introduces a different kind of spatial layering.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #219

stops.whyHere: Horizontal white lines rule across vertical color strokes, holding yellow and orange masses above while blue strokes fall below; the two movements meet without resolving.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The canopy-like yellow of the previous work reappears, but now white ruled lines impose a horizontal order that the color beneath refuses to respect.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #36

stops.whyHere: A dark figure sits amid billowing white loops on a blue-lavender ground while a warm solar disc occupies the upper left — the surrounding air carries as much visual weight as the figure within it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The loose yellow masses of the previous work condense here into a single disc at upper left, and the open field below the figure carries the same diffuse, cloud-like quality the earlier work spread across its whole surface.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #65

chapters.title: Faces and Fields
chapters.introduction: Four works where a face is surrounded by color zones or enclosing marks that divide or reframe it, plus one abstract field showing what remains when the face is absent.

stops.whyHere: Yellow floods the upper field while olive pools below, splitting the face across two tones; a faint blue rectangle floats over the center like a second, cooler layer pressing in from outside.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The solar disc from the previous work has expanded here into an entire yellow field that the face must occupy rather than observe.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #296

stops.whyHere: Dense black hatching buries the face's surface while a yellow loop arcs outside the form, pulling attention around the figure rather than into it.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous face was split by a surrounding color field, this one is buried under hatching — the pressure has moved from the field inward to the surface itself.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #189

stops.whyHere: A broad fan of pale light pushes from the left across gold and ochre bands while a heavy black arc holds the right edge — an abstract field of light against weight, with no face present.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The yellow loop outside the previous figure becomes here a full light source pushing across the frame; the figure has disappeared, leaving only the tension between radiance and dark mass.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #82

stops.whyHere: A gold-olive mass fills the frame, its surface built from crossing scribble lines; a diagonal light beam cuts across the upper left while a dark cavity below reads as tense against the calm background spirals.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The broad light fan of the previous work narrows here into a single diagonal beam, and the mass it strikes is denser and more resistant than the open bands it crossed before.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #84

chapters.title: Light as Enclosure
chapters.introduction: Four works where light does not simply illuminate but surrounds or structures the forms inside it, making the lit space feel sealed rather than open.

stops.whyHere: A form sits sealed inside a dome while gold rays push outward from behind it; the enclosure reads as both lit from within and pressed upon from without, the floating pale circles softening neither reading.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The diagonal beam of the previous work has expanded here into a full radial burst, and the form it surrounds is now literally enclosed rather than merely struck.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #78

stops.whyHere: The image divides between a dark layered left mass and a blazing yellow-gold right field where two white discs burn; red blocks at the bottom sit heavily against that upper light.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The dome's contained radiance opens here into an unenclosed split — light and dark occupy separate halves rather than one surrounding the other.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #180

stops.whyHere: Two hard light beams slice through layered nested rectangles, pulling the eye from a dense scribbled left edge toward glowing ovals that read as sources rather than reflections.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two white discs of the previous work reappear here as two beams cutting through structure rather than burning within an open field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #75

stops.whyHere: Two white-hot rectangles anchor the composition while zigzag lines spread outward in yellow and cyan; a dark compressed cluster at upper left sits in contrast to that brightness.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The beams of the previous work have condensed into two fixed rectangular sources, and the surrounding marks now radiate outward from them rather than crossing them.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #73

chapters.title: Geometry and Scatter
chapters.introduction: Two works where surrounding space is organized by bars, arches, and zigzag lines that hold or release the forms sitting inside them.

stops.whyHere: A horizontal bar with oval recesses anchors the upper field while downward triangles and surrounding zigzag lines read as noise holding the central forms in charged suspension.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The two glowing rectangles of the previous work reappear here as oval recesses in a machine-like bar — the light sources have become inset forms, and the surrounding scatter has become more organised.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #74

stops.whyHere: Two diagonal beams slice through a field of zigzag borders and nested rectangles; glowing spiral cores inside the arched form hold still against all that surrounding movement.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The bar and triangles of the previous work give way here to diagonal beams crossing a similarly dense field — the geometry shifts from horizontal to diagonal, and stillness moves from the bar into the spiral cores.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #76 cash lightning
